intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians perform as the square transforms from a daytime market into a spectacular open-air food festival at dusk. Wander the labyrinthine souks of the ancient medina, haggling for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles just steps from your accommodation.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp in Merzouga
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for an unforgettable camel trek into the Sahara. Ride at sunset as the dunes glow amber and rose, then spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp under a canopy of stars. Enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake at dawn for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes — a once-in-a-lifetime desert experience.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back in time with a self-guided or local-guided tour of two of Marrakech's most significant historical landmarks. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with its intricate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. A short walk away, the Saadian Tombs — sealed for centuries and rediscovered in 1917 — house the ornate mausoleums of the Saadian dynasty, offering a profound glimpse into Morocco's imperial past.
experiences.location: Kasbah & Riad Zitoun districts, Medina, Marrakech

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class with a Local Family
experiences.description: Begin your morning at the vibrant Mellah spice market to hand-select fresh ingredients — saffron, ras el hanout, preserved lemons, and more. Then join a local Marrakchi family in their home kitchen to learn the art of preparing authentic dishes such as slow-cooked lamb tagine, harira soup, and honey-drenched bastilla. Sit down together to enjoy the feast you've created, paired with fresh-baked khobz bread and mint tea.

experiences.name: Ait Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Day Trip
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day excursion from Marrakech over the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Ait Benhaddou — a stunning fortified mud-brick village used as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, palm groves, and Berber villages, offering rich historical and cultural context to your Moroccan journey.
experiences.location: Ait Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~80-100 MAD) or a pre-booked airport transfer to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat, located in the heart of the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In transit
meals.lunch: N/A – In transit
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a quick snack from a late-night street stall near Jemaa el-Fna square (5-15 MAD for msemen flatbread or a harira soup cup). Many stalls stay open past midnight.

day_by_day.notes: Keep small change (MAD) ready for the taxi. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance since arrival is late. The Medina streets are narrow – a hotel staff member may meet you at a nearby landmark to guide you in.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then walk to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5-minute walk from the hotel) to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, storytellers, and snake charmers. Explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only, free) and stroll through the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the Marrakech souks – the labyrinthine markets surrounding Jemaa el-Fna. Explore the spice souk (Rahba Kedima), the dyers' souk, and the leather goods area. Practice your bargaining skills. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate tilework and carved cedar wood – a must-see for history lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at dusk when it transforms into a massive open-air food market. Eat dinner at the communal food stalls (stall numbers 1-100) – try harira soup (5 MAD), kefta brochettes (15-20 MAD), and merguez sausages. Watch the acrobats, musicians, and storytellers for free entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Café Arabe area or hotel breakfast – mint tea, msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), and hard-boiled eggs (~20-30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap local eatery near the souks – try a tagine or couscous set menu at a workers' restaurant for 30-50 MAD (ask locals for 'restaurant populaire')
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna night food stalls – full meal with soup, brochettes, bread, and fresh juice for ~50-70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – you'll cover 5-8 km on foot. Keep your bag close in the souks. Bargain everything to 30-50% of the initial asking price. The Ben Youssef Madrasa is a short walk from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a 19th-century grand vizier's palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, painted ceilings, and lush courtyards. Arrive early (opens 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) to explore its distinctive architecture and the historic Lazama Synagogue (small donation appreciated).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved royal necropolis from the 16th century, just a 10-minute walk from Bahia Palace. Then explore the Kasbah neighborhood and the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) – a once-magnificent palace now in atmospheric ruins, great for history buffs. Climb the ramparts for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mellah's evening market for local snacks. Have dinner at a traditional Moroccan restaurant in the Medina. Return to Jemaa el-Fna for evening tea and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Street-side café near the hotel – café au lait and a croissant or beghrir (semolina pancakes with honey) for ~15-25 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack lunch near El Badi Palace – a sandwich with kefta or tuna from a local bakery/snack shop (~20-30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Haj Brik or similar local Medina restaurant – a full Moroccan set menu (soup, tagine, dessert) for ~60-90 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Bahia Palace, Saadian Tombs, and El Badi Palace form a convenient triangle – all walkable. A combined visit takes about 4-5 hours. Wear modest clothing when visiting religious or palace sites.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00-7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a shared group tour or budget minibus (book through your hotel or a local agency – 1-day Sahara tours from Marrakech are not feasible; this is a 2-day/1-night trip to Zagora or a 3-day trip to Merzouga). For budget travelers, book a shared 2-day/1-night tour to Zagora Sahara (~400-600 MAD per person including transport, camel ride, and desert camp). Depart through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude) with stunning Atlas Mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar/fortified village) en route – a famous backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the ancient mud-brick citadel (entry ~10-20 MAD). Continue through the Draa Valley with its palm groves and kasbahs toward Zagora.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara near Zagora (Erg Chigaga or Erg Lihoudi dunes). Mount camels for a sunset ride into the dunes (~30-45 minutes). Watch the sunset over the Sahara – a breathtaking experience. Settle into a budget desert camp (included in tour price) with a Berber dinner, traditional music around the campfire, and incredible stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure – bread, jam, mint tea (~20 MAD or included in hotel)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop in the Atlas Mountains or Ouarzazate – tagine or sandwich (~40-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp package – traditional Berber meal: harira, tagine, bread, mint tea (~included or ~80-100 MAD if separate)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sahara tour at least 1-2 days in advance through your hotel or a reputable agency. Compare prices – shared group tours are significantly cheaper than private. Bring warm layers (desert nights can drop to 5-10°C in March), sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf for the camel ride. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise to watch the dawn light paint the Sahara dunes in gold and pink – one of the most magical experiences of the trip. Take a short morning walk in the dunes. Enjoy a simple Berber breakfast at camp (mint tea, bread, honey, argan oil). Begin the return journey to Marrakech after breakfast (around 7:00-8:00 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey through the Draa Valley and Atlas Mountains. Optional stop at a local argan oil cooperative to learn about production (free to visit, no obligation to buy). Stop in Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Africa' – for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios (entry ~50 MAD) if time permits, or simply walk around the kasbah area.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (around 18:00-19:00). Rest at Hotel Aday. Take a gentle evening stroll through the Medina to decompress. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp – Berber breakfast with mint tea, bread, and local spreads
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate or the Atlas Mountains – tagine set menu (~50-70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Medina restaurant near the hotel – a simple, hearty meal of couscous or pastilla (~50-80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long (5-7 hours with stops). Stay hydrated and bring snacks for the road. If you feel adventurous, Friday evening is a great time to visit Jemaa el-Fna as it's especially lively after Friday prayers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~100 MAD for garden + Berber Museum) – a stunning botanical garden with cobalt-blue buildings, exotic plants, and the excellent Berber Museum inside. Arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) to avoid crowds. The garden was restored by Yves Saint Laurent and is one of Marrakech's most beautiful spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gueliz neighborhood (New City) – a contrast to the Medina with French colonial architecture, art galleries, and modern cafés. Visit the Marrakech Museum of Photography and Visual Arts (free or low entry) if open. Browse the weekly Mellah market or the Bab Doukkala area for authentic local shopping – spices, dried fruits, and olives at market prices (much cheaper than tourist souks).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina for a final evening in the souks. Pick up last-minute souvenirs – leather goods, argan oil, spices, or Berber jewelry. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking Jemaa el-Fna for a memorable final evening view.

meals.breakfast: Café near Majorelle Garden – café au lait and pastries (~25-35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Gueliz neighborhood café or sandwich shop – a modern Moroccan lunch for ~40-60 MAD. Try Café du Livre or a local snack bar.
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant overlooking Jemaa el-Fna (Café de France area or similar) – tagine or mixed grill for ~80-120 MAD with a view

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is a 20-minute walk or short taxi ride from the hotel (~20-30 MAD). Saturday is market day in many neighborhoods – great for authentic local shopping. The Gueliz area has ATMs if you need to replenish cash.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Take a slow, leisurely walk through the Medina one last time – visit any spots you missed or revisit favorites. Stop at the Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful morning sit. Browse the morning market near Bab Agnaou gate for fresh produce and local life. Pick up any final souvenirs or gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final mint tea at a traditional café. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) in a beautifully restored 19th-century palace if you haven't already – it houses Moroccan art and artifacts. Pack up at Hotel Aday and check out. Head to the airport with ample time (allow 1.5-2 hours before departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert adventure, history, and incredible food.

meals.breakfast: Final traditional Moroccan breakfast at a Medina café – mint tea, msemen, honey, and amlou (~20-30 MAD). Savor it!
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel before checkout – a bowl of harira and bread (~15-20 MAD) or a quick sandwich (~20-30 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight (budget accordingly – airport prices are higher, ~80-150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and plan checkout accordingly. Petit taxis to the airport cost ~80-100 MAD (negotiate before getting in). Keep some MAD for the taxi and any last purchases. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if required. A wonderful budget Morocco trip – total estimated daily spend (excluding tours): 200-350 MAD/day (~$20-35 USD).

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour hanout (corner shop) close to the hotel in Derb Sidi Bouloukat

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Confirm your hotel has late check-in arranged. Exchange a small amount of currency (MAD) at the airport for immediate needs. The Medina streets can be confusing at night — share your hotel address in Arabic with your taxi driver.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, begin exploring the heart of the Medina. Visit the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, storytellers, and snake charmers. Then walk to the nearby Koutoubia Mosque (exterior view) and stroll through the surrounding gardens. Head into the souks: explore Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market), and Souk Haddadine (blacksmiths).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD entry) — a stunning 19th-century riad palace with intricate Moroccan tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Lazama Synagogue. End the afternoon at the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD entry) for panoramic views and a sense of Marrakech's imperial past.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into a massive open-air food market. Watch the acrobats, musicians, and henna artists. Dine at one of the food stalls (stalls 1–100 are popular) — try harira soup, merguez sandwiches, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Aday or a nearby café — traditional Moroccan breakfast with msemen (flatbread), amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, and mint tea (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café des Épices near Place Rahba Kedima — rooftop terrace with tagines and sandwiches (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls — budget-friendly and authentic (~60–100 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 5–8 km today. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a small bag and be mindful of pickpockets in crowded areas. The Medina is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a visit to the Saadian Tombs (~70 MAD entry) — 16th-century royal mausoleums rediscovered in 1917, featuring exquisite mosaic and stucco work. Then head to the Madrasa Ben Youssef (~70 MAD entry), one of the largest Islamic colleges in North Africa, with breathtaking Andalusian-Moroccan architecture. Explore the adjacent Museum of Marrakech (~50 MAD) housed in a 19th-century palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi ride (~20 MAD) to the Majorelle Garden (~150 MAD entry) — a stunning botanical garden with cobalt-blue buildings designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Visit the adjacent Berber Museum inside the garden. Afterward, explore the Gueliz (Ville Nouvelle) neighborhood for a change of pace — browse art galleries and modern boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Moroccan hammam experience at a mid-range hammam near the Medina such as Hammam Dar el-Bacha (~150–250 MAD for full scrub and steam). Afterward, enjoy a relaxed dinner at a rooftop restaurant in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Patisserie des Princes near Jemaa el-Fna — fresh pastries, coffee, and Moroccan pancakes (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Café Arabe in the Medina — Moroccan-Mediterranean fusion in a beautiful riad setting (~120–180 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Le Jardin restaurant in the Medina — set in a lush courtyard garden, serving classic Moroccan dishes like pastilla and lamb tagine (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden online in advance — it sells out, especially in spring. The hammam is a quintessential Moroccan experience; bring flip-flops and a change of clothes. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (~18–24°C), ideal for garden visits.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (~7:00 AM) on a pre-booked shared or private transfer toward the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley route (Ouarzazate → Zagora or Merzouga). The drive to Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes) takes approximately 8–9 hours with stops. First stop: the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass through the High Atlas Mountains — dramatic scenery and Berber villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Stop at the Kasbah Taourirt (~30 MAD entry), a UNESCO-listed earthen fortress. Browse the nearby artisan cooperative for handmade carpets and pottery. Continue driving through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) and the dramatic Draa Valley with its ancient kasbahs and palm groves.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga (~18:00–19:00). Check into a mid-range desert camp or guesthouse (pre-booked). Mount camels for a 45-minute sunset camel trek into the dunes. Watch the sunset over the Sahara — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner at camp under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure — packed or quick (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate — Moroccan set menu with harira, tagine, and bread (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — included in most camp packages; expect couscous, tagine, Berber bread, and mint tea (~150–200 MAD if not included)

day_by_day.notes: Book your desert camp and transport in advance — recommended options near Merzouga include Sahara Desert Camp or similar mid-range camps (~400–700 MAD/night including dinner and breakfast). Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Pack sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (~6:00 AM) for a magical dawn camel ride or walk to the top of the dunes to watch the sun rise over the Sahara. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Explore the village of Merzouga on foot — visit local Gnawa musicians, a fossil shop (the region is rich in trilobite fossils), and interact with nomadic Berber families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional activities near Merzouga: visit the Dayet Srji salt lake (flamingo spotting in spring), take a 4x4 excursion to remote dune areas, or visit the Khamlia village to hear traditional Gnawa music performed by descendants of sub-Saharan slaves. Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via the Todra Gorge route.
day_by_day.evening: Stop and overnight in the Todra Gorge area (Tinghir) — a dramatic canyon with 300-meter-high rose-colored rock walls. Take an evening walk through the gorge as the light turns golden. Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Tinghir.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — included; bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch or stop at a local café in Merzouga village (~60–80 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your guesthouse in Tinghir or a local restaurant — try mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) or a vegetable tagine (~100–150 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the late afternoon light. The drive from Merzouga to Tinghir is approximately 3–4 hours. If time allows, a short hike into the gorge at dusk is highly recommended. Confirm your guesthouse booking in Tinghir in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk through the Todra Gorge before the tourist crowds arrive — the light is spectacular. Continue the drive back toward Marrakech via the Dades Valley (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs). Stop at the Dades Gorge for photos of the winding road and dramatic rock formations. Visit the Aït Benhaddou UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) — one of Morocco's most photographed sites and a famous film location (~30 MAD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Aït Benhaddou thoroughly — cross the river on stepping stones, climb to the top of the ksar for panoramic views, and visit local artisan workshops selling pottery and carpets. Continue the final stretch back to Marrakech (~2.5 hours from Aït Benhaddou). Arrive in Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Aday, freshen up, and enjoy a final evening in the Medina. Visit the Mellah spice market for last-minute souvenir shopping — saffron, argan oil, ras el hanout spice blend, and rose water are excellent buys. Enjoy a leisurely farewell dinner at a traditional Moroccan restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Tinghir guesthouse — traditional Moroccan spread (~40–60 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Lunch near Aït Benhaddou at a local restaurant with views of the ksar — tagine and salad (~100–130 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dar Zitoun or similar mid-range riad restaurant in Marrakech Medina — try a full Moroccan feast: pastilla, lamb tagine with prunes, and bastilla au lait for dessert (~180–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Tinghir to Marrakech via Aït Benhaddou is approximately 5–6 hours total with stops. Start early to make the most of Aït Benhaddou. Aït Benhaddou has been used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia — a fascinating cultural and historical stop.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow breakfast and last walk through the Medina. Visit any missed sites: the Musée de Marrakech, the tanneries (best viewed from leather shop rooftops — free with a guide tip), or simply wander the quieter back alleys of the Medina. Pick up final souvenirs in the souks — leather goods, babouche slippers, lanterns, and Moroccan ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina. Visit the Koutoubia Gardens for a peaceful stroll. If time allows, take a short calèche (horse-drawn carriage) ride around the ramparts of the Medina (~150–200 MAD for 45 minutes). Head to the airport with ample time — allow 1.5–2 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert, history, and food across one of the world's most captivating destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday or a nearby café — msemen with honey and argan oil, mint tea (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Nomad restaurant near the Spice Square — modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views (~130–180 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the Medina by taxi (~80–100 MAD). Confirm your departure terminal in advance. Morocco's currency (MAD) cannot be exported in large quantities — spend remaining dirhams or exchange back at the airport. Tipping is customary: 10–15 MAD for small services, 20–50 MAD for guides.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Hotel Aday in the heart of the Medina (Derb Sidi Bouloukat). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea and light snack prepared by the riad. Rest and settle in.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Light welcome spread at Hotel Aday upon arrival — traditional Moroccan pastries, olives, harissa, and fresh mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport pickup in advance with a premium private transfer service (e.g., a Mercedes V-Class or similar). Hotel Aday is located in a narrow Medina alley — luggage porters will assist from the nearest vehicle drop-off point. Keep Day 1 light; the real adventure begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the riad rooftop terrace. Begin a guided private walking tour of the Medina — explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive. Visit the 16th-century Koutoubia Mosque gardens, then head into the labyrinthine souks: spice market (Rahba Kedima), leather tanneries viewpoint, and the artisan copper and lantern quarters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Bahia Palace — a stunning 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with ornate tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the Saadian Tombs, a hidden royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring exquisite Andalusian-Moroccan architecture. End the afternoon with a curated visit to a premium argan oil cooperative for a sensory demonstration.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop of a boutique bar overlooking the Medina skyline (e.g., Nomad Rooftop or similar). Dinner at a top-tier Marrakech restaurant — Le Foundouk or Dar Yacout — for a multi-course traditional Moroccan feast in a candlelit palace setting.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday rooftop — msemen flatbreads, amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, honey, cheese, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant in the Medina — modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views; try the lamb pastilla and harira soup
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout or Le Foundouk — lavish multi-course Moroccan dinner featuring bastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and traditional pastries with orange blossom water

day_by_day.notes: Book a private licensed guide for the Medina walking tour (half-day). Reserve dinner at Dar Yacout well in advance — it is one of Marrakech's most celebrated dining experiences. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Ben Youssef Madrasa — one of the largest Islamic colleges in North Africa, featuring breathtaking Moorish architecture, intricate zellige tilework, and carved stucco. Explore the adjacent Museum of Marrakech housed in a 19th-century palace. Stroll through the Mouassine neighborhood, one of the Medina's most atmospheric quarters, visiting the Mouassine Fountain and a curated selection of high-end concept stores and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée YSL Marrakech). The cobalt-blue garden, once owned by YSL, is a botanical sanctuary of rare cacti, bamboo groves, and fountains. The museum showcases the designer's deep love affair with Morocco through rotating exhibitions. Afterward, visit the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the historic El Badi Palace ruins — a 16th-century sultan's palace with panoramic terrace views.
day_by_day.evening: Authentic hammam and spa experience at a premium establishment such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Royal Mansour Spa — enjoy a traditional black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant in the Gueliz district for a fusion of Moroccan and Mediterranean flavors.

meals.breakfast: Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday — beghrir (semolina pancakes with honey butter), fresh fruit platter, yogurt, and spiced coffee
meals.lunch: Café de la Poste in Gueliz — a Marrakech institution with a French-Moroccan brasserie menu; try the grilled brochettes and Moroccan salad spread
meals.dinner: Comptoir Darna — a legendary Marrakech supper club with Moroccan-French cuisine, live music, and belly dancing performances in an opulent setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the YSL Museum tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly. Reserve the hammam session for late afternoon (around 16:00–18:00) for a relaxing pre-dinner ritual. Comptoir Darna is lively and theatrical — perfect for an immersive evening.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the journey to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dunes) — approximately 8–9 hours of scenic driving through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) for panoramic photos and fresh mountain air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley — a stunning landscape of ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and red-rock gorges. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (fortified village), one of Morocco's most iconic landmarks and a famous film location (Gladiator, Game of Thrones). Enjoy a private guided tour of the ksar with a local expert. Continue driving through the Valley of Roses (Dadès Valley) and the Gorges du Dadès.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a luxury desert camp or boutique lodge near Merzouga (e.g., Scarabeo Camp, Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp, or similar). Camel trek at sunset into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the golden light on the towering sand dunes is extraordinary. Arrive at a private luxury Berber camp for a traditional dinner under a canopy of stars, with live Gnawa music around a campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast prepared by Hotel Aday — croissants, fruit, cheese, and thermos of coffee/tea for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, Berber bread, and fresh-squeezed juice
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber feast at the luxury desert camp — harira soup, mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous with seven vegetables, and Moroccan pastries under the stars

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — depart by 07:00 to arrive comfortably before sunset. Hire a reputable private driver with a luxury 4x4 (Toyota Land Cruiser or similar). The Aït Benhaddou stop is a highlight — allocate at least 1.5 hours. Pack a light jacket as desert nights can be cold in March (temperatures can drop to 5–10°C).

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise camel or quad bike ride to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes — watching the Sahara sunrise from the highest dune is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a guided walk with a local Berber guide to learn about desert survival, nomadic culture, and the unique ecosystem of the Sahara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Merzouga and the nearby Dayet Srji lake (seasonal flamingo habitat). Explore a traditional Berber family home for an authentic cultural exchange and mint tea ceremony. Drive to the Erfoud fossil workshops — the region is famous for its 350-million-year-old marine fossils embedded in black marble. Begin the scenic return journey westward, stopping at the Todra Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300-meter-high rose-colored rock walls.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a luxury kasbah hotel in the Tinghir or Ouarzazate area (e.g., Kasbah Tamadot, Kasbah du Toubkal, or Berbère Palace Ouarzazate). Enjoy a candlelit dinner on a terrace overlooking the valley with traditional Moroccan music.

meals.breakfast: Full Berber breakfast at the desert camp — msemen, honey, argan oil, fresh dates, eggs, and mint tea as the sun rises over the dunes
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the camp — Moroccan sandwiches, olives, fruit, and pastries enjoyed at the Todra Gorge
meals.dinner: Dinner at the luxury kasbah — slow-cooked lamb shank tagine with saffron and preserved lemon, Moroccan mezze, and bastilla au lait for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Set an alarm for 05:30 to catch the sunrise — it is the most magical moment of the desert experience. Bring a scarf or shemagh for the dune trek (wind and sand). The Todra Gorge is best visited in the afternoon light when the canyon walls glow amber.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the kasbah — enjoy the pool, spa, or a yoga session on the terrace with Atlas Mountain views. Depart mid-morning for the return journey to Marrakech via the scenic Route of the Kasbahs. Stop at the Ouarzazate film studios (Atlas Studios) — the largest film studios in the world, used for Lawrence of Arabia, Babel, and many others — for a fascinating private tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley palm groves and stop at the Tamnougalt Kasbah — a 16th-century fortified village with a knowledgeable local guide. Cross back over the High Atlas via the Tizi n'Tichka pass, stopping at a Berber cooperative for premium saffron and handwoven carpet shopping. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Aday. Freshen up and head to the Djemaa el-Fna square at dusk — the square transforms into a magical open-air theater with storytellers, musicians, snake charmers, and food stalls. Enjoy a final premium dinner at one of Marrakech's finest restaurants — La Maison Arabe or Dar Moha — for an unforgettable farewell meal.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the kasbah hotel — fresh pastries, local honey, cheese, fruit, and freshly brewed Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch at a highly regarded local restaurant near Ouarzazate — chicken tagine with olives and preserved lemon, Moroccan salads, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Dar Moha — set in a stunning 1930s villa with a pool garden; Chef Mohammed Fedal's creative Moroccan haute cuisine is legendary; try the pigeon pastilla and lamb with ras el hanout

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Ouarzazate to Marrakech is approximately 3.5–4 hours. Depart by 13:00 to arrive comfortably for the evening. Reserve Dar Moha well in advance — it is one of the most sought-after tables in Marrakech. The Djemaa el-Fna at dusk is unmissable — bring cash for the entertainers.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in Marrakech. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the riad. Last-minute premium shopping in the souks — visit a curated selection of high-end artisan boutiques for handmade leather goods (Maison Artisanale), bespoke Moroccan jewelry, hand-painted ceramics, and luxury argan oil products. Visit the Mellah spice market for saffron, ras el hanout, and rose water to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — optional visit to the Menara Gardens, a serene 12th-century olive grove with a reflecting pool and Atlas Mountain backdrop, perfect for a peaceful final stroll. Check out from Hotel Aday and arrange private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Carry the memories of the Medina's labyrinthine alleys, the silence of the Sahara dunes, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday rooftop — a full spread of Moroccan breads, honey, amlou, fresh orange juice, and mint tea with views over the Medina
meals.lunch: Al Fassia Aguedal — an iconic Marrakech restaurant run entirely by women, serving authentic Fassi (Fez-style) Moroccan cuisine; try the lamb with caramelized onions and prunes
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or light meal before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the airport transfer and check-in process. Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy — arrive early. Declare any food items (spices, argan oil) at customs if required. Consider tipping your private guide, driver, and hotel staff generously — it is customary and greatly appreciated in Morocco.
